..
Mostly island-effect convection is seen across the Marianas this
afternoon. Winds remain light and variable across Saipan, allowing
the convection to continue over the island, with locally heavy
showers possible for the next couple of hours. Otherwise, expect 
only isolated showers through the night. Winds are strong enough to
push most of the showers off to the north of Guam, with one
thunderstorm developing right along the Guam and Rota coastal 
waters border. Overall, expect a drier pattern across the CNMI over 
the next several days, though the light winds do lend to the chance 
of another round of island convection for Saipan and, to a lesser 
extent, Tinian again on Thursday. For Guam, the effects of the 
monsoon trough look to move into the waters and over the island at 
times through the weekend, along with a risk of thunderstorms. Heavy 
rainfall does not look likely over the next several days.

Marine...
Fairly benign marine conditions are expected over the next several
days, with seas slowly subsiding to around 3 feet for the weekend.
Light to gentle winds will prevail.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 91W was just upgraded to Tropical Depression 25W (TD 25W) by 
the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) this evening. TD 25W, is 
centered west-northwest of Saipan near 16.2N 137.9E, moving 
northwest. Latest satellite data shows a consolidating Low-Level 
Circulation Center (LLCC) with increasing convection near and N of 
the center. TD 25W remains in a favorable environment for 
development, with low vertical wind shear, good equatorward outflow 
and warm sea surface temperatures. Additional development of TD 25W 
is expected as the tropical cyclone moves to the northwest and away 
from the region.

For more information on Tropical Depression 25W, see bulletins 
issued by JTWC under WMO headers WTPN31 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
A monsoon trough is located just north of Pohnpei that is expected to
drift just far enough south to bring scattered showers and isolated
thunderstorms by late tonight and tomorrow and continuing to waiver
in and out for the rest of the forecast period. Gentle to moderate 
winds will continue into the weekend with gustier winds possible with
any thunderstorms. 

Kosrae looks to remain dry most of the week as it remains far south 
of the trough. Precipitable water values are still above two inches
however, so shower coverage could briefly become scattered at times,
particularity Thursday night. Gentle to moderate winds are expected 
to decrease by Thursday night, potentially becoming light by
Saturday. 

Models have been overestimating rainfall for Majuro but isolated
showers may increase to scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
overnight. Winds look to decrease from gentle to moderate starting 
tomorrow, becoming light by Friday. Intermittent periods of scattered
showers and isolated thunderstorms will remain possible all week as 
a series of weak troughs moves through the Marshall Islands.

Combined seas of 5 to 6 feet tonight will become 4 to 5 feet for all
islands for most of the forecast period with no significant swells 
expected at this time. Some choppy seas will be possible near heavier
showers and thunderstorms.

Western Micronesia...
TD 25W will continue to lift to the northwest and away from the 
region, and conditions will slowly improve through late this week at
Yap and Palau. Monsoonal inflow into 25W that has brought heavy 
rainfall, gusty winds, and locally choppy seas to portions of Yap 
State and Palau the last couple of days will also lift northward as 
the tropical cyclone moves away from the region. That being said, 
locally heavy showers will still be possible through Thursday at Yap,
especially near heavier showers and thunderstorms. Higher-end 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will be possible through
Thursday and conditions are expected to improve thereafter with 
shower chances dropping to isolated by Saturday evening at Yap and by
Friday evening at Palau. Gentle to moderate southwest winds will 
continue at Palau and Yap through Friday and become mostly gentle 
this weekend. Occasional gusts to 25 kt will continue to be possible 
at Yap through Thursday, especially near heavier showers and 
thunderstorms. Combined seas of 4 to 5 feet will continue through 
Thursday and begin diminish a foot or two this weekend. 

Mostly drier weather is expected to persist at Chuuk through Friday
with shower chances topping out around 30 percent. Shower chances
will increase this weekend to higher-end scattered, along with some
isolated thunderstorms being possible. Light to gentle west to
southwest winds will continue through this weekend. Generally benign
marine conditions are expected at Chuuk with combined seas topping
out around 4 feet through Thursday, dropping to around 3 feet by this
weekend.
